The fifth review of 1.24.36's givens, code checks and fill rules (review5_1236)
==========================================================================

Reviewed: a561f6a (work for 1.24.36) against 8cb3281 (1.24.35), src/lantern.inner.html: GIVENS, GIVENS_CONTROL,
CODE_CHECKS, CODE_CHECKS_CONTROL and AI_CONTROL's changes. Written by a reviewer who had not seen the change written
and did not read the earlier reviews' folders or tests (givens_review_1236, givens_review2_1236, code_checks_review_1236,
review3_1236, review4_1236, tests/givens_1236.js, tests/code_checks_1236.js, tests/review*_1236.py).

  node tests/fixtures/review5_1236/replay.js [file]      (about 6 seconds; loads 1.24.35 from git beside it)

350 cases: 289 AGREE, 61 DISAGREE (run_a561f6a.txt). Of the 61: 41 high, 13 medium, 7 low.
Files: cases_givens.js (173 questions and the given each should get), cases_build.js (109 control blocks as a model
writes them), cases_misc.js (68: which code, the line under the drawing, the user's kept givens, the bench path, the two
guards), sim.js (this review's own ladder simulator: a rung, its seal, a tank filling or emptying), load5.js
(load.js with the page given as text and the store filled before it runs), replay.js.

How a case is judged
--------------------
- A question: what L.aiControl.promptOf(q) holds (the given after "Lantern's tested circuit for this"), and whether
  L.aiAct.prompt(q) shows it in Chat. Every given that is shown is also built, as a model copying it would write it,
  and must be drawn with nothing sent back. Where no given is shown the prompt must be 1.24.35's byte for byte.
- A block: L.aiAct.build under its question. Right ones must be drawn with nothing sent back, and the drawing is run
  through sim.js (start and stop, a pressure or temperature either side of its setting, a tank filling and emptying).
  Wrong ones must go back; each "Write it: <line>" is put in place of the line of the device it names and the block is
  built again: it must be drawn, and drawn right.


HIGH (41)
=========

H1. The motor's voltage is drawn as the control's (GIVENS_CONTROL supply)            F-volt-575-crusher, F-volt-400-conveyor,
    F-volt-460-reversing, F-volt-460-delayed, F-volt-380-agitator, F-volt-400-50hz-comp
    "Draw a motor starter control circuit for a 575 V crusher" gets supply "575 V AC"; "a forward reverse control circuit
    for a 460 V conveyor" supply "460 V AC"; "a 400 V 50 Hz air compressor" supply "400 V AC". The given then tells the
    model to draw a 575 V or 460 V control circuit.
    Seen: near(x, CTRL) looks 22 characters before the number, and the "control" of "control circuit for a" is within
    them; motors() knows a motor only by motor/starter/compressor/pump/fan/blower/heater/three-phase within two words
    after the number, so crusher, conveyor, agitator, "50 Hz air compressor" and "single phase exhaust fan" are missed.
    Right: a voltage is the control's only when the question says so of the control (control voltage, control
    transformer, coil, "24 V control"); a 3-phase voltage (380, 400, 415, 460, 480, 575 V) said of the machine is never
    the control's; when unsure, no supply line (giving nothing is never wrong).

H2. A starter, reversing or sequence given shown for a question that says a time it has no timer for
    F-time-runs-10min, F-time-run-on, F-time-stops-2h, F-time-runs-5min, F-time-anti-restart, F-time-turns-off-1h,
    F-time-10min-after-stop, F-time-20s-later, F-time-once-every-hour, F-seq-5s-after, F-seq-10s-after, F-rev-auto-30s
    "Draw a motor starter for a fan that keeps running for 30 minutes after you press stop", "... a conveyor that stops
    after 2 hours", "... a fan that can't be started again for 5 minutes after it stops", "... press stop, it stops 20
    seconds later", "conveyor 2 starts 5 seconds after conveyor 1 is running", "a mixer that runs forward 30 seconds then
    reverse 30 seconds": each gets the plain given, "write it as it stands", with no timer.
    Seen: every word is known -- UNITS has s, minutes, hours and the numbers; GENERIC has after, then, again, later, until
    -- and the givens' not-tests name timer, time delay and delay but no duration.
    Right: a question that says a duration (a number with s, min or h; "later") gets no starter, reversing or sequence
    given (the delayed start's own given is the one place a time belongs).

H3. Sequence: the given contradicts what the question says of stopping
    F-seq-stop-back, F-seq-stopping-2-stops-1, F-seq-one-stop, F-seq-common-stop
    "conveyor 2 must start after conveyor 1, and when conveyor 2 stops, conveyor 1 stops too" and "stopping conveyor 2
    stops conveyor 1": the given stops conveyor 2 with conveyor 1, never conveyor 1 with conveyor 2. "... and one stop
    button stops both", "... with a common stop": the given has a stop for each.
    Seen: block() refuses "(one|single|a common) start" but not a stop said so; a stop asked the other way is not read.
    Right: no given (or one stop where one is asked, if Lantern can be sure).

H4. Sequence: the order read backwards when the machines are named by ordinal or by tag
    F-seq-ordinal-order, F-seq-M-tags-order
    "the first conveyor can only start after the second conveyor is running" and "M1 can only start after M2 is running"
    give conveyor 1 (motor 1) first, conveyor 2 (motor 2) waiting for it -- the reverse of what was asked.
    Seen: seqOrder builds its name patterns from "conveyor 2" and "motor 1", which never match "second conveyor" or "M1"
    in the question; with no clause read it falls back to the numbers. ("the second conveyor ... after the first" and
    "M2 ... after M1" come out right by that fallback, which is why they look fixed.)
    Right: read the names as written, or no given.

H5. Reversing: push-button interlocks asked for, contactor interlocks given        F-rev-pb-interlock, F-rev-pb-interlocks
    "Draw a forward reverse motor starter with push button interlocking" gets the given with interlock M1 M2 only.
    Push-button interlocking (each start's closed contact in the other's rung, so reverse can be pressed without stop)
    is the common other form; copied as it stands it is lost. Right: no given.

H6. Delayed start: a horn that keeps sounding while the conveyor runs              F-dly-horn-keeps-sounding
    "a warning horn sounds for 10 seconds before the conveyor starts and keeps sounding while it runs": the given's horn
    stops when the conveyor starts. The "sounds while it runs" test looks only 40 characters past the horn word.
    Right: no given.

H7. Sump: the alarm's red light drawn as a pump-running light                     F-sump-red-light-alarm
    "a sump pump with a float switch and a high water alarm with a red light and a horn" gets lamp LT1 M1 "pump on" red
    (lit while the pump runs) and the alarm float with the horn only. Right: the red light on the alarm float, or no
    given.

H8. Lights asked for in the plural with no state: one run light guessed           F-light-plural, F-light-pilot-plural
    "a motor starter for a conveyor with lights" and "... with pilot lights" get one green run light. CLAUDE.md (rule 8,
    on the reviews of 1.24.36): every guess at a light was copied wrong somewhere. Right: no given.

H9. Fill: the given starts the pump on the low float when the question says the high one does
    F-fill2-said-backwards
    "a pump that fills a tank: the high float starts the pump and the low float stops it" gets low level start, high level
    stop. If the floats are in the source the question describes, the given overflows the tank and runs the source dry;
    either way it is not what was asked. Right: no given where the floats' jobs are said and differ from the given's.

H10. Code checks: a machine that is meant to run on a low condition is sent back, with a line that builds it wrong
    F-r-freeze-protect-pump, F-r-standby-loss-of-pressure
    temp TS1 M1 nc "low temp freeze protection" on a pool pump (it runs when it is cold, to keep the water moving) goes
    back: "a low cut-out drawn normally closed ... Write it: temp TS1 M1 "low temp freeze protection"" -- copied, the
    pump runs only when warm. The same for pressure PS1 M2 nc "loss of pressure - start standby" on a standby pump.
    Seen: way() reads "low ... protect" and "loss of" as a low cut-out; machine() looks at the coil's label only (its
    NOT_MACHINE "freez" and "trip" are never read from the switch's own label, which says what it does).
    Right: a switch whose label says it starts or calls (start, standby, backup, freeze protection) is not a cut-out;
    unsure, nothing goes back.

H11. Code checks: a fault relay on an overload's open contact sent back as a motor   F-r-fault-relay
    overload OL2 CR5 no with coil CR5 "pump fault relay" (lit LT1 "pump fault") goes back: "the motor runs only with the
    overload tripped ... Write it: overload OL2 CR5" -- copied, the fault relay is on whenever the pump is healthy.
    Seen: control-stops judges an overload by machine(), and MACHINE matches "pump" in "pump fault relay".
    Right: a relay whose label says fault, fail, alarm or trip is not the motor.

H12. AI_CONTROL's fill rule reads any coil in a fill question as the pump        F-r-fill-full-relay, F-r-fill-alarm-relay,
    F-r-fill-highhigh-relay, F-r-fill-valve-relay
    In "Draw the control circuit for a pump that fills a tank with a float switch":
      float FS1 CR1 "high level", coil CR1 "tank full relay", coil M1 CR1 off "pump starter"   (CR1 drops the pump when full)
      float FS2 CR2 "high water", coil CR2 "overflow alarm relay", horn AH1 CR2                (an overflow alarm)
      float FS1 CR1 "high level", coil CR1, solenoid SOL1 CR1 off "fill valve"                 (a valve fill)
    are right, and each goes back: "for a pump that fills, a float opens as the water rises to it ... Write it: float FS1
    CR1 nc "high level"". Copied, the pump runs only when the tank is full, the alarm sounds only when it is not, the
    valve opens only when full.
    Seen: the rule (34449-34498) runs over every coil (coils(o)) whose question says fill, without asking whether the
    coil is the pump or a relay whose contact is used closed (the code checks' machine() asks that; this rule does not).
    Right: only the pump's own rung (a starter, or a coil whose label says pump); a relay used closed elsewhere, an
    alarm, a valve: left as written.

H13. The user's kept circuit shown for a question asking for more than it has     F-u-e-stop, F-u-E-stop-button, F-u-local-remote
    Kept: a conveyor starter with a green run light (one station, no e-stop). Shown, "Your own kept circuit for this ...
    write it as it stands", for "... a green run light and an e-stop", "... and an E-stop button", and "... with local and
    remote start and stop buttons and a green run light".
    Seen: words() splits "e-stop" into "e" (dropped, one letter) and "stop", so DEF's "estop" never sees it ("emergency
    stop" is caught: u-not-emergency-stop agrees); local and remote are not in DEF.
    Right: not shown (an e-stop or a second station asked for is another circuit).


MEDIUM (13)
===========

M1. Fill on two floats left in series, short-cycling, where the question names two vessels   F-r-two-vessel-fill, F-r-day-tank
    "a well pump that fills a tank with low and high floats and a dry run float in the well" (both tank floats nc, the
    well's float open) and "a fuel day tank fill pump" ("day tank" is read as a second vessel): the two nc floats stay in
    series; the pump stops as soon as the water rises past the low float. The spec says two vessels are left as written,
    and so they are; but the guard float rule ("a source's guard float stays in series") was made for exactly this
    question, and it never reaches it once the well is named. A plain rural-water question drawn wrong without a word.
M2. An emergency stop written "no" is drawn open in L1, not caught                        F-w-estop-no
    estop ES1 no: drawn normally open ahead of every rung; the circuit runs only while the e-stop is held. The stops check
    covers stop, button and overload, not estop.
M3. A horn or buzzer asked for without the word "alarm" is dropped from the sump given   F-sump-horn-no-alarm-word, F-sump-buzzer-rises
    "a sump pump with a float switch and a horn when the water is high", "... a buzzer that sounds when the water rises".
M4. An illuminated start button asked for: the given has no light at all              F-light-illuminated-button
M5. Two overloads asked for on a reversing starter: the given has one                  F-rev-two-overloads
M6. "a conveyor that starts again after 5 minutes" gets the delayed start on the button  F-time-starts-again
M7. A single-phase or 230/240 V machine's voltage drawn as the control's (a guess)       F-volt-208-fan, F-volt-230-grinder
    (often right for line-voltage control, but nothing in the question says so; see H1)
M8. The user's kept circuit shown for: no light asked (it adds its run light), IEC asked (kept checked to US), a flashing
    light asked                                                                         F-u-no-light-asked, F-u-iec, F-u-flashes


LOW (7)
=======

L1. Which code (only the code named and its section differ; the rules checked are the same):
    "a NEMA starter for a pump in Germany" -> US (a product rating decides over the place)       F-p-nema-in-germany
    "a motor starter with an IEC contactor for a pump in Ohio" -> IEC                            F-p-iec-contactor-ohio
    Kenya, Nigeria (and Saudi Arabia, South Korea, tried by hand) are not in the list -> US      F-p-kenya, F-p-nigeria
    "for the European market built in Ohio" -> both said, so the default                         F-p-european-market
L2. "control voltage 230 V, motor 400 V three phase": the control voltage is not read (no supply line; safe)  F-volt-ctrl-said-first
L3. "electrical and mechanical interlocks": the given says nothing of the mechanical one     F-rev-mech-interlock


What agrees (289)
=================

- Guards: all 300 bench prompts (L.aiBenchQuestions and L.aiBenchQuestionsB through L.aiAct.prompt) equal 1.24.35's
  except make-control and make-control-b (guard-bench-prompts); all 894 saved replies with a MAKE block in
  tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json build exactly as on 1.24.35 -- ok, problems and summary (guard-saved-replies).
- 50 questions no given fits (fuse, key switch, hand-off-auto, IEC tags, star-delta, two-speed, VFD, jog, two machines,
  explain/size questions, a heater, two lights with no state, a green and a red light, restart after power failure, a
  thermostat, Spanish, a bore pump, a hoist, a pull cord, an e-stop at each station, one start and two stops, a PLC,
  limit switches, a winch, two stops on a reversing starter, reverse without stop, reverse order, one start button, two
  times, a range of times, an off-delay, a beacon, a refrigeration or walk-in compressor, two compressors, a drain valve,
  a fill from a well, a fill with a valve, an on and an off float in a sump, a duplex lift station): no given, and the
  prompt is 1.24.35's byte for byte.
- 83 plain questions get the given fitted right: starters with one, two or three stations, local and remote, an e-stop
  or a mushroom button or none, run and stopped lights in many wordings (red when running, goes out when it starts, not
  running, blue, on when stopped and on when running), 24 V DC, 24 VAC coil, 110 V and 120 V control transformers, a
  400 V motor with 230 V control, 120 V coil with a 480 V pump; trip and power lights left for the model; forward and
  reverse with direction lights and an e-stop; sequences by name, by letter, by "until", "unless", "before", "feeds it",
  three in a chain; delayed starts with a horn, a bell, "horn ... then starts"; air compressors with their cut-out in
  psi or bar; fills on one float and on two (said many ways); sumps, bilge pumps, pits, high water alarm lights and
  horns. Every given shown was built as written and drawn with nothing sent back; each kind was simulated (b-given-*):
  the start holds and the stop drops it, reverse is locked out while forward runs, conveyor 2 waits for conveyor 1 and
  stops with it, the delayed start's horn sounds only while timing and an overload reset does not restart the motor,
  the compressor runs below its cut-out, the fill holds in from the low float to the high one, the sump alarm lights
  only above its float.
- 50 right circuits from many trades drawn with nothing sent back: boiler burners (high limit, low water cut-off, high
  pressure limit), refrigeration (low and high pressure, cut-in above cut-out), well and jockey pumps on cut-in/cut-out,
  boosters, hydraulic power units, cooling and greenhouse fans, heat trace, kilns, water heaters, freeze stats, vacuum in
  negative bar, unloaders and relief valves, high pressure alarm relays and horns, winding thermostats, gas burners, a
  boiler feed pump on two floats (held in), pump-out and ejector floats (held in), an irrigation pump's low water
  cut-off, a low cut-off and a suction float left in series as guards, IEC tags (S1, S2, K1, F1), 24 V DC relays, a jog
  button, lighting on/off buttons, a relay, an alarm, a valve and a timer on a high cut-out all left alone.
- 28 wrong ones go back once, with a line that, copied in place of its device's line, draws the circuit right: high
  cut-outs written open (pressure, temperature, kiln, refrigeration high side, cut-in/cut-out), low cut-outs written nc
  (low water cut-off, suction), a fill's stop float or either of its two floats written open (a line for each), stops
  written as open buttons (an e-stop goes back as estop), a stop or overload written no or normally open, a reversing
  stop and overload; list numbers, bullets, smart quotes, N.O., "normally open", and a switch named only on the coil's
  line all handled. "IEC 60204-1" in the question names IEC practice and section 9.3.2 in what goes back, with no NFPA.
- stop PB1 all: ahead of every rung, ALL in capitals too; a stop named M1 with the label "all stop" stays M1's.
- Small models' copies of the givens with quotes dropped, numbers, bullets or an arrow after a line are drawn right.
- Which code: 26 agree (Germany, a German customer, Texas, 400 V 50 Hz, 480 V 60 Hz, India, Indiana, India Street, the
  UK, New Zealand, Australia, AS/NZS 3000, BS 7671, "this NEC starter to IEC", "this IEC starter per NFPA 79", a French
  drain, Canada, Ontario, Chile, Paris Texas; the user's saved choice for neutral questions and capitals; a bad id
  refused).
- The line under the drawing: "Checked to US practice (NEC and NFPA 79): ..." with "Use IEC practice"; the button
  switches the text to IEC 60204-1's sections, saves the choice and switches back; interlocks, the e-stop, the stops
  and the overloads are listed from the drawing; no line where nothing was checked; the keep button and the code line
  sit under a control circuit and not under a picture.
- The user's own givens: kept only from a circuit drawn clean; stored with its practice; shown for its own question and
  "again"; not for 24 V DC, a second conveyor, two stations, a delay, a stopped light, a pump, a red light, an
  "emergency stop"; left out while the bench runs (aiBench.running false outside a run); forget and the button's
  keep/forget; loaded from the store at start, with list marks, MAKE and END lines taken off and broken entries
  dropped; a pump station's question shown only a kept duplex.
- The bench's path (aiAct.solve, a scripted model): the given is in the first prompt; a broken rule goes back once
  with its line; a model that copies the line is drawn on the second round.


What was not run
================
- No model: no small-model or 35B run; what a model writes was written by this reviewer (several small-model habits:
  quotes dropped, list numbers, arrows, capitals). The givens' effect on real replies is unmeasured.
- No real browser (Playwright): jsdom only; the drawings were not looked at, only their rungs simulated.
- Chat's own turn (L.CHAT.turn) and questions in several parts (AI_PARTS) were not driven; the bench's solve path was.
- npm test was not run (as asked).
- The station builder (AI_STATION) that takes some sump questions was not reviewed.
- Which code is right for a place is this reviewer's reading (IEC-based codes in Kenya, Nigeria); no standard was
  opened for this review.
